messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

It's been nearly a decade since the hurricane ravaged her small coastal town, yet for Emilia, the memories still linger like an open wound. She recalls the sound of the front door bursting open, the howling wind, and the feeling of utter chaos as her home was torn apart. The trauma has left an indelible mark on her life, one that she struggles to shake off even in the quiet moments. The slightest creak of a door opening or slamming can transport Emilia back to that fateful day. Her heart racing, she is convinced that disaster is lurking around every corner, waiting to strike again. The world, once a predictable and safe place, has become a treacherous landscape where anything can happen without warning. Conversations about loss and tragedy only serve to reinforce this notion, making her dwell on the what-ifs and the could-haves. Even the smell of alcohol, a common scent in the aftermath of the storm, is enough to trigger a cascade of memories she would rather forget. Emilia's attempts to regain control over her life have led her down a path of rumination and compulsive behavior. She spends hours poring over news articles and documentaries about natural disasters, convinced that if only she had been better prepared, things might have turned out differently. Her graphic design work, once a source of joy and creativity, has become a chore as she becomes fixated on reorganizing her workspace and perfecting every detail. This excessive attention to detail is an attempt to impose order on a world that feels increasingly capricious. Despite the passing years, Emilia's memories of the hurricane remain vivid yet strangely disconnected from her emotions. There are times when she can recall the events with eerie clarity, only to feel as though she is observing someone else's life. The story of what happened feels almost surreal, like a narrative she has constructed rather than lived through. And yet, in other moments, the memory feels agonizingly present, as if the storm could sweep back into her life at any moment. Emilia's sense of injustice and outrage still simmers just below the surface. The lack of accountability for the disaster's aftermath and the perceived failure of authorities to prevent such tragedies only serves to fuel her feelings of resentment and powerlessness. This perception of a world that is fundamentally unfair has become a self-reinforcing cycle, driving her maladaptive strategies and further entrenching her negative appraisals. As Emilia navigates this complex web of emotions and memories, she finds herself increasingly withdrawn from the world around her. Her relationships with loved ones suffer as she becomes more isolated, fearful of being overwhelmed by her own thoughts and emotions. It is only when she is confronted with the possibility of losing her husband to illness that Emilia realizes she can no longer continue down this path alone. With a sense of trepidation, she begins to seek help, hoping to break free from the cycle of fear, rumination, and avoidance that has come to define her life. Emilia's eyes well up with tears as she finally acknowledges the depth of her pain and the overwhelming sense of injustice that still gnaws at her soul. It is this moment of raw vulnerability that marks the beginning of her journey towards healing, one that will require her to confront the shattered remains of her old self and slowly rebuild a new narrative – one where trauma no longer defines her every waking moment.
